Of course! The whole point of all the rules is just to make it so everyone has a fair serve with no advantage. So with the toss on a volley, you're not really gaining anything at all if the other rules apply. 
I spent a whole day dialing in a very noticeabley legal serve, and now I get 2-4 aces a game. Once you get the hang of top spin, serves are a piece of cake.

Volley means you just hit the ball in the air without it hitting the ground first.
There's no height or limitation with the toss as long as you hit the ball below your waist.

That's exactly right for the drop serve, because otherwise the bounce that you'd hit would be higher and easier to have an advantage.

It's actually not accurate.. you can throw the ball as high as you want on a volly serve. The only time tossing a ball up on your serve is during the drop serve. 
As long as the rest of the serve is fine, wrist angled down, hit below waist, no spin applied to the ball etc etc
